question.worked_solution:
Either the positive or negative of the expression inside the absolute value must be equal to the right-hand side of the equation.

So, we set up the two corresponding equations and solve them independently:

- If $|3-\frac{2}{3}y|=3-\frac{2}{3}y,$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|3-\frac{2}{3}y| & =5 \\ 3-\frac{2}{3}y & =5 \\ -\frac{2}{3}y & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $-\frac{3}{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{3}y & =2 \\ (-\frac{3}{2})\cdot (-\frac{2}{3}y) & =(-\frac{3}{2})\cdot (2) \\ (\cancel{-\frac{3}{2}})\cdot (\cancel{-\frac{2}{3}}y) & =-\frac{6}{2} \\ y & =-3.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $|3-\frac{2}{3}y|=-(3-\frac{2}{3}y),$ we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}|3-\frac{2}{3}y| & =5 \\ -(3-\frac{2}{3}y) & =5 \\ -3+\frac{2}{3}y & =5 \\ \frac{2}{3}y & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $\frac{3}{2}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{3}y & =8 \\ (\frac{3}{2})\cdot (\frac{2}{3}y) & =(\frac{3}{2})\cdot (8) \\ (\cancel{\frac{3}{2}})\cdot (\cancel{\frac{2}{3}}y) & =\frac{24}{2} \\ y & =12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solutions are $y=-3$ and $y=12.$
